spatial_claims.claim: ABC is a circle; CD is a straight line through the centre; AB is a chord not through the centre; E is the intersection of CD and AB on segment AB
F is the centre of circle ABC, so F lies on line CD (since CD passes through the centre); FA and FB are radii
Triangles FEA and FEB are non-degenerate (F is off line AB since AB does not pass through centre F)
Angle FEA equals angle FEB by SSS congruence (I.8)
FE stands on line AB making equal adjacent angles FEA and FEB, so both are right angles (Def 1.10)
Triangle FEA is right-angled at E with hypotenuse FA; Pythagorean theorem gives FA² = FE² + AE²
Triangle FEB is right-angled at E with hypotenuse FB; Pythagorean theorem gives FB² = FE² + EB²

configuration_map: Points: A, B on circle ABC (chord endpoints); E is the intersection of lines CD and AB; F is the centre of circle ABC lying on line CD. Key relationships: F is NOT on line AB (since AB does not pass through the centre, and E is the unique intersection of the two distinct lines CD and AB). Therefore triangles FEA and FEB are non-degenerate. F is distinct from E. In Part 1, E is the midpoint of AB (given), and the proof shows the angle at E is right. In Part 2, the angle at E is right (given), and the proof shows E is the midpoint. The AI uses I.47 (Pythagorean theorem) for Part 2 instead of Heath's I.5/I.26 approach, but the spatial configuration supports both methods equally well.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The configuration (circle with centre F, chord AB not through centre, diameter CD meeting AB at E) is simple and well-determined. The non-degeneracy of triangles FEA and FEB is guaranteed by AB not passing through the centre. The AI's use of the Pythagorean theorem (I.47) in Part 2 instead of Heath's I.5/I.26 approach introduces no spatial issues — both right triangles are properly formed with the right angle at E and the radii as hypotenuses.
